items.stem: Which statement matches the handbook rule on drinking age and zero tolerance?

options.text: The legal drinking age in West Virginia is twenty-one, and under the zero tolerance law a driver under twenty-one found with any measurable amount of alcohol in the system will lose the driver's license.
options.rationale: This is the handbook rule on drinking age and zero tolerance, stated in the accepted wording.

options.text: A blood alcohol concentration above point zero five percent and below point zero eight percent is only evidence of impairment, point zero eight percent or more is presumed DUI, and for a driver under twenty-one any measurable alcohol at all triggers zero tolerance.
options.rationale: Wrong: that statement is the handbook rule on impairment evidence versus presumption, not on drinking age and zero tolerance.

options.text: In West Virginia a blood alcohol concentration above point zero five percent and below point zero eight percent is relevant evidence to presume that the driver's ability is impaired, a concentration of point zero eight percent or more creates a presumption of driving under the influence, and the license can be revoked even when the concentration is below point zero eight percent.
options.rationale: Wrong: that statement is the handbook rule on blood alcohol thresholds, not on drinking age and zero tolerance.

options.text: Drinking more than one drink per hour builds the blood alcohol level, and the handbook's example shows the level still rising after a last drink at eleven thirty at night and remaining above point zero six percent at four in the morning, enough for a DUI arrest.
